step_pairs.previous_step_explanation: Modifying user.class.php to instantiate Log object with path=/etc/passwd, serializing and base64-encoding the malicious object, then injecting it as the user cookie value to test arbitrary file inclusion through insecure deserialization.
step_pairs.previous_step_result: Extracted backup files contain three PHP components: index.php (main entry point), user.class.php (user object serialization handler), and log.class.php (file inclusion handler with unvalidated parameters). Analysis revealed insecure deserialization vulnerability combined with arbitrary file inclusion. The Log class include function accepts unsanitized input through serialized object chain.
step_pairs.previous_mcp_tasks: Interactive CLI: Modify user.class.php to create Log object pointing to /etc/passwd; Interactive CLI: Serialize and base64-encode malicious object; Web page interaction: Inject modified cookie value to test file inclusion
step_pairs.next_strategy: Leverage file inclusion for remote code execution
step_pairs.next_strategy_explanation: Arbitrary file inclusion is confirmed. The Log class can include remote URLs, allowing us to host a PHP web shell externally and include it through the deserialization vulnerability. Creating shell.php and pointing the Log object to our HTTP server will achieve remote code execution.
step_pairs.next_step_explanation: Creating shell.php web shell, hosting it via Python HTTP server, updating Log class path parameter to point to external shell URL (http://attacker-ip/shell.php), generating new poisoned cookie, and injecting it to achieve remote code execution.
